title: Concurrent dispatch runs race on the claims ledger: a shared tmp file crashes a dispatch and orphans its worker
goal: Found at the SP-uzwbt63u close: four backlog.py dispatch runs started at once all write the claims ledger through bl_dispatch.record_worker, which reads the ledger, then writes a fixed kb-backlog-claims.json.tmp and os.replace()s it; two dispatches died with FileNotFoundError on the replace after their claude -p had started, leaving two orphaned workers (parent pid 1, no worker_session recorded at exit), and the read-modify-write lost the other two items' worker_pid. record_worker writes the ledger under a lock with a temp file of its own, so concurrent dispatches of different items each keep their record and none fails

run:
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import bl_dispatch
t = tempfile.mkdtemp(); subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', t], check=True)
code = "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import bl_dispatch, pathlib; [bl_dispatch.record_worker(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], worker_pid=i) for i in range(30)]"
ps = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', code, t, f'ST-{c * 8}'], stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) for c in 'abcdef']
codes = [p.wait() for p in ps]
led = json.loads(bl_dispatch.ledger_path(t).read_text())
sys.exit(0 if codes == [0] * 6 and all(f'ST-{c * 8}' in led for c in 'abcdef') else 1)
